utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to all. May I have the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. For the Office of the Prosecutor, I'm Tom Hannis along with Gerard Dobbyn and our case manager, Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, joined by our expert Mr. Mladen Bajagic appear for the Stanisic Defence. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, for Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the witness takes the -- well, I see these she's been escorted into the courtroom, we've been alerted that there may be a minor preliminary matter? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, regarding the next witness I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- an application I want to raise, I thought I'd do it before he came in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Ms. Hanson. I remind you that you are still on your oath before I would invite I think it was Mr. Zecevic who had some further questions. Or was it Mr. Pantelic? Pantelic, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Further Cross-examination by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Hanson. I have just one question for you: Were you aware that sometimes mid-April in 1992 the Presidency, Bosnian Serb Presidency, adopted the decision of the state of imminent threat of war in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think microphone is off. Now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that subsequently on the Republican Assembly session in Banja Luka, on, I believe, 12th of May, 1992, this decision was actually subsequently formalised?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that Assembly session, I believe, but I'm not aware of that particular verification but I can well imagine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I don't have further question for Ms. Hanson. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So. Thank you for your assistance, Ms. Hanson. You are now released.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I believe at this point now is the appropriate time to deal with the admission of Ms. Hanson's report, which has been marked for identification up to this point? It's Exhibit P434. And I would be asking that it be tendered into evidence now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, just for the record, Defence would like to stand with its previous reasoning in objections with regard to the admission of the report. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do you have a position, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This is a joint application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, the decision of the Chamber is that the report having been previously marked for identification is now admitted as an exhibits. We are not unmindful of the objections which were taken initially by counsel for the Defence, but in our view, the only course open is to admit the report fully as an exhibit and all of the issues which have been identified in the process of cross-examination now affect the weight which the Chamber will at the end of the day give to that report. Thank you. So the report would now be, having been tendered, is now admitted and marked as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. The next witness will be Christian Nielsen. He is our expert on the police. I did have one matter I had indicated through an e-mail that I wanted to raise concerning one document, which is 65 ter number 1862. It's a document that is described as the RS MUP payroll for April 1992 for the special platoon in the Serbian Ministry of Affairs. It had previously been listed in Mr. Nielsen's report at footnote 273 in connection with paragraph 220 of his report, but the ERN listed is incorrect by one digit. In his report it is listed as FI20-1877. The actual document is FI20-0877. I wanted to bring this to your attention and substitute the correct document. The issue of the special platoon of police from Sokolac is something that I think is mentioned in our pre-trial brief, it's something that the Defence is well aware of. We were discussing charts showing the organisation of the various units, and I know Mr. Zecevic took issues with where we were trying to place that platoon on the organisational chart. So it's not a matter of notice, I don't think, it's just a matter of correcting the record and that's why I applied to substitute FI20-0877 for the document that was previously listed, FI20-1877.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We do not oppose, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thanks to my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So the correction may thus be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The one matter I'd like to raise further before we call in the witness has to do with just timing and tendering. It's my understanding of Your Honours' previous indications with the expert witness Hanson that footnoted documents in the expert's report, if they are on the Prosecution's 65 ter list, will be admitted as part of the report if you accept the report; am I correct in my understanding about that? Okay. Because there were too many documents in the footnotes for me in the time available to go through with Mr. Nielsen each one of them, and what I propose to do at the end of his evidence, if you are satisfied to accept his report, then I want to tender all the footnoted documents that are also on our 65 ter list. But for purposes of numbering, I think it makes sense to do it at the end of his evidence, then I can provide a list to the Registry officer indicating which ones are in his report and have a 65 ter number. If that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That would be the best solution and the best way forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And if I may again, just for clarification, repeat the Chamber's position on this. The exercise that the Chamber has been trying to perform is an attempt to limit the number of associated documents that are normally following in the wake of the expert reports to what is really necessary and relevant to the case. And so we expect the parties, and this goes also for the Defence when it's going to be their turn, to identify in advance which of the footnoted documents in the expert reports that they would wish to have admitted into evidence once the report itself is admitted. So I hope this clarifies the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It does. And I have to apologise for not having that list with me now at the beginning of his evidence. And for purposes of the record, what I intend to do, if I show him documents now, I'm going to refer to the 65 ter number, or in some cases the exhibit number for those that are already in. And lastly, there is a document that is marked as 65 ter number 10083 which is described erratum sheet for Mr. Nelson's report. I don't know if Your Honours have seen that yet, but we went through and identified some typographical errors, et cetera, and I don't know the best way procedurally to do that. I'm going to ask him if he has looked at it and it reflects the changes he wanted to make, and if he wants you to consider that as part of his total report, and then I would tender it if that's the appropriate way to proceed. I see Mr. Zecevic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't -- I believe we don't take the issue with the last thing what you suggested. What I wanted just to procedural matter, we would appreciate, and I think it would be for the benefit of all in, specifically the Trial Chamber, that when Mr. Hannis is providing the list of the report, the 65 -- so the list of the documents which are in the report and are on the 65 ter list, the cross-reference to the footnote must be given as well because otherwise it would be really enormous task to identify which document goes with what. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That's a very good idea, thank you, and I would ask Mr. Hannis to comply.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree. And we'll certainly do that. That will be helpful to us as well as you and my learned friends. Thank you. I have nothing further now, and I guess I'm ready to call in Mr. Nelson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you wish to give us a heads-up on where we are with this report between the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we've discussed, Mr. Hannis and myself, as you know, we took the -- we filed an objection on Mr. Nielsen, which we still maintain. That's the first. The second thing is, Your Honours, Mr. Nielsen's report is basically a foundation for the pre-trial brief of the Office of the Prosecutor with which we take the issue. I tried to -- to the best of my abilities, I tried to identify the parts where -- and I can give the indication to the Trial Chamber, and I thought that maybe the best way would be that I go through the executive summary of the document, and then I will provide you with a certain -- with a certain E numbers in the executive summary with which we basically do not take the issue, or I should indicate that we take the partial issue with some of the -- the numbers in the executive summary. So to that end we don't take the issue with E1, E2, E5, E10, E22, E23, and partially we take the issue with E6, E8, E9, E17, E18, E24. The rest we most definitely take the issue with. I hope I was of some assistance. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. This is useful for us to know before we hear the witness. So that means that the paragraphs in the executive summary that you have not singled out are the paragraphs with which you do take issue; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We take the issue with everything else in all other paragraphs which I didn't mention, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I inquire, those which he takes issue partly with, if he could identify which parts, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you will see in the cross-examination, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Would you be good enough to read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, you may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, welcome to the Tribunal, welcome back I should say --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- I know that you have been employed here before. Mr. Nielsen, you are being called as an expert witness for the Prosecution to share with the Chamber your knowledge of the MUP, and for this purpose, the Prosecution has been granted six hours to take you through your expert report. And the Defence have asked for eight hours; is that correct, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was nine, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Nine hours, sorry, that's true. And the Zupljanin Defence has asked for four hours, if I'm not mistaken. So this is how the testimony will proceed. The Prosecution will start out and take us through your expert report, and then the floor will be given to the Defence with the number of hours that I have just indicated, and then the Prosecution will have an opportunity for re-examination after the Defence cross-examination, and in the end the Judges may have some questions for you. You have been given a pseudonym, ST-092, but as there are no issues of protective measures that apply in your case, we will just refer to you by your name. For the record, I'd like you to state your name and your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Christian Axboe Nielsen and I was born on the 12th of September, 1973.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Dr. Nielsen. I would like to begin by showing you 65 ter number 10084. This is your CV, Doctor. And one of the questions I would like to ask: On the CV it indicates you are presently teaching at the university in Denmark?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I see that one of the courses you teach is in the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. I teach the language that is referred to in this courtroom as B/C/S at the university in Denmark.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you have a PhD in what?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I have a PhD in history.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's your CV that was provided by you; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender that document, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when did you last -- oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document shall be given Exhibit P454. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When did you last work as a full-time employee for the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I left the ICTY at the end of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to refer you next to 65 ter number 10082. This is tab 75 in the hard copy of the binders, but I will tell you this is your report entitled "The Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs, Genesis, Performance and Command and Control 1990 to 1992." Can you tell us when you began writing that report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I began writing the report in September 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And why were you writing that report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I arrived at the OTP at the ICTY in June 2002 and was immediately tasked to examine documents concerning the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs, or RS MUP, and a couple of months later, approximately in September 2002, I was tasked to write an expert report or, rather, a report that became an expert report on that subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how did you go about preparing that report? Could you describe briefly for us your methodology and your sources?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: My methodology quite simply was to examine as many documents pertaining to the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs and its predecessor ministry, the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina's Ministry of Internal Affairs. That, at some points, required when I identified significant gaps in OTP's collection of such documents, also travelling to the field and searching for additional documentation. Most of the sources in the report that the court has before it are original documents of the RS MUP, that is to say, the overwhelming majority of sources that I quote in the report are the documents of RS MUP itself or of its predecessor ministry to which I referred.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In connection with gathering or supplementing that collection, did you take an active role in the actual gathering of some of these documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, beginning in November 2002 [realtime transcript read in error "1992"], I asked for permission to travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina to rectify what I identified as significant gaps in the holdings of the OTP as pertaining to documentation of MUP, and on several occasions starting in November 2002 and until the end of my employment - and I should mention that I was at OTP in two different periods - I collected, I would estimate, tens of thousands of pages of documentation relevant to this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in writing your report -- I am sorry I see Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I think we have a unclear situation here. It's page 11, line 7, starting with November 1992, I think it's not correspond the fact what witness maybe mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, could you clarify for us: It's on the transcript as "... beginning of November 1992, I asked for permission to travel to rectify what I identified as gaps in the holdings of the OTP ..." was that 1992 or some other year?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I believe that I said 2002. That was definitely the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And with regard to the documents you reviewed in preparing your report, did you work with originals in the B/C/S or from translations or both?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I always did my analysis based on the B/C/S originals of the documents. I was only very rarely presented with the translations, usually when staff members who did not speak B/C/S had questions about the content of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I take it then that you are fluent in reading, writing, and understanding B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us when and how you obtained that proficiency?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I began studying B/C/S in 1994 and took several courses at university level in Germany and in the United States, and I subsequently spent a very considerable amount of time in the former Yugoslavia where I had the opportunity to further develop my proficiency in the language.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And in compiling the report, was that your report, this exhibit, was that prepared only by you or was it written by anyone else?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I'm the sole author of the report, and I'm also the sole person who decided to -- which documents would be included in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report at paragraph 4 in the introduction you say that the aim of this report is to provide an analysis of the establishment of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska. Is that an accurate description of what you were trying to do?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in paragraph 6, you indicated that your report was done on the basis of available RS police, military, political and other related documentary materials. Is that an accurate description of what you based your report on?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You are aware that a substantial amount of material has come into the OTP since you left?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show you next Exhibit 10083 -- 65 ter number 10083. And this is described as the erratum sheet for your report. You are familiar with this document that was prepared to reflect some errors, typographical -- primarily typographical errors in your report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And having had a chance to review that, are you satisfied that those changes should be made to your report, and would you like the Trial Chamber to consider this erratum sheet as part of your report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I think since the time that was prepared, you indicated to me yesterday that there was one additional item you had discovered. In reviewing your prior testimony in the Krajisnik case, you indicated that you needed to make a change to paragraph 82 of your report. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And could you indicate what that change is?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Certainly. In the first paragraph of -- excuse me, in the first sentence of paragraph 82 of my report, I state: "Earlier in the day the president of the Assembly Momcilo Krajisnik had strongly hinted that the establishment of a Bosnian Serb police force was imminent." I was asked on cross-examination in Krajisnik and corrected, but failed to subsequently correct in the addendum or the erratum sheet, the fact that the person who made that comment was actually the then president of the SDS Radovan Karadzic and not Momcilo Krajisnik. Therefore the sentence should read: "Earlier in the day, Radovan Karadzic had strongly hinted that the establishment of a Bosnian Serb police force was imminent."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours I would like to indicate I will move to tender his report and the erratum sheet at the end of all his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For now I have a couple of more questions about your report, Dr. Nielsen. With regard to the footnoted documents, what can you tell us generally about the authenticity of those documents? When and where and how were they obtained?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: The footnoted documents, certainly those that pertained to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, either the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs or its predecessor in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina stemmed from a number of document collections that we had in the Office of the Prosecutor. I was not personally involved in collecting all of these documents. I do know in most cases where those documents were collected, as I had an opportunity to review that information. Another substantial, very substantial portion of the documents, original documents cited in this report were, as I stated earlier, documents that I collected personally at the offices of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republika Srpska between 2002 and 2004, and as such, I am quite certain that these documents are indeed authentic and original documents of the ministry in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the course of preparing your report, can you give us any estimate of approximately how many documents you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: It's always very difficult, whether with this report or a work of history, to reconstruct precisely how many pages one has reviewed or documents. However, I would certainly say that I reviewed in excess of 200.000 pages of documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the course of reviewing that, did you come across any documents that were doubtful to you in some way concerning perhaps authenticity or source, and if so, how did you handle those?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: On very rare occasions, I did encounter a few documents that were, in my opinion and based on my analysis, of questionable provenance. In any case where that was a matter of doubt, I chose to not rely upon those documents unless it could be ascertained as an analyst beyond my own reasonable doubt that these were indeed authentic documents. That is to say, any documents that are cited in this report, are done so on the basis of my analysis that they are indeed authentic documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as a category of documents, I would ask you about media sources. I think we all in the courtroom have some trepidation about relying on media resources given the fact that there were three different sides in this conflict with different motivations, and I think it would be fair to say that there was a lot of propaganda from all three sides in this conflict. How did you deal with media sources and when did you include any of those?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I included relatively few media documents, that is to say open-source documents in my report. Most of those in the report pertain to, I think the period in March 1992 immediately preceding the break-up of the Bosnian Ministry of Internal Affairs. And I did so in that case to reflect the quite vociferous public debates ongoing at that point in time. I certainly agree that I would not attach as much analytical value to those documents as I do to the documents that stem from the Ministries of Internal Affairs, but I did provide them, as it were, to also give a flavour of the kind of public debates that were ongoing at the time concerning RS MUP and its predecessor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I mentioned earlier that you testified previously in the Krajisnik case. That's at this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as an expert?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On what?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: On the same subject, that is to say on the basis of a slightly earlier version of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Any other testimonies as an expert on the police in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: No, not to date. However, I should mention, as is reflected in my CV, that I have been retained by the Canadian Ministry of Justice and I'm expecting to testify in a case in Vancouver next year that is pertaining to a former member of the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you also listed and scheduled to testify as an expert in any other cases in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes. I am currently scheduled to testify on the basis of another report in the case of Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic, and I have also been notified that I will testify on the basis of the present report in the case of Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, regarding your report, you have, I think, on page six, you've listed some acronyms that you rely on, and at footnote 1 on page 6, you make a reference to the RS Republika Srpska and the SR BiH, the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You indicate that the -- the date that the name officially changed to Republika Srpska was apparently August 12th 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That's correct. It appeared as an amendment on August 12th and the name change took effect officially in August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I have to confess that sometimes I may not be precise in making the reference, so I hope you'll understand if I say Republika Srpska and we are talking about something in March, you understand I'm referring to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or you can correct me when I make that mistake, okay?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I think that such, if you permit, loose usage actually conforms quite well to the usage that's seen in the documents themselves and by the participants in these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. A couple of matters [Microphone not activated] of terminology before I go into the substance of the report at page 39 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At paragraph 39, which is at page 20 of the English in your report, and paragraph 41 subparagraph 4, which is at page 21 in the English. I don't know if you can advise of the B/C/S page for those paragraphs. Do you have the B/C/S version in front of you or the English?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I have the English version in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You make reference to OSUP. Can you tell us briefly what the OSUPs were?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: The OSUPs were Municipal Secretariats for Internal Affairs. These existed until 1990 when a new Law on Internal Affairs in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina came into effect at which point they were replaced by the SJBs, the stations of public security.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on subparagraph 4 under paragraph 41, you make reference to this proposal that: "The Serbian Assembly and government could declare void the 1989 amendments to the Law on Internal Affairs. This would restore the old Municipal Secretariats of Internal Affairs SUP ..." Would it be fair to say that that refers to the OSUPs, the predecessor municipal OSUPs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. The municipal -- the word "municipal" is "opstina" or "obcina" [phoen] in B/C/S, and that is the O in OSUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you explain me to the difference between the OSUPs and SJBs that we have been talking about in this case, if any?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Very general generally, I would say the predominant difference between the OSUP and its successor the SJB is that the municipality and officials at the municipal level had a much more considerable say in the operation of the OSUP than they did once the SJBs came into functioning. That is to say, that the beginning of the SJBs represents, as it were, somewhat mild centralisation of Internal Affairs, with more power or more, let's say, yes, more power, more control placed within -- vested within the ministry itself rather than at the municipal level with municipal level officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the OSUPs were funded by the municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, to a considerable extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what about the SJBs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: The SJBs also represented a change in the sense that hence forth the financing was more internal to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One other term I want to ask you about is referred to at footnote 157 on page 39 of the English in your report. It's a footnote to paragraph 110, regards the term authorised official. Can you tell us a little bit about what an authorised official was in the RS MUP in 1992.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, as I suggest here, I provide a definition actually taken out of the Serbian dictionary of police law. I quote a policemen, a professional member, worker, official, we might say employee of the Ministry of Internal Affairs who, in the implementation of internal affairs, has particular obligations and authorisations for seeing in the laws on criminal procedure the Law on Internal Affairs and other regulations, and as I note in the same footnote, from this definition, as well from as from the definition given for police officer in the same dictionary, it emerges that every authorised official in the Secretariat Ministry is considered to be a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you aware of some of the privileges that attach to holding a position of authorised official in the MUP as contrasted to other employees of the MUP who were not authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of some of these privileges. Certainly one of the most germane ones is the ability exercised by authorised officials operating in the field to carry fire-arms, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Make arrests?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And with a prior MUP witness I had this conversation, and I think I confused him or perhaps he confused me, there was a reference to the term "operative" in describing certain MUP employees. Are you familiar with that term?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I'm certainly familiar with the term "operative." It's not a term in the sense of authorised official. That is usually used in public security. It's a term that I'm much more familiar with as being used in documents on state security and usually refers to what one in English would call an agent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Would operatives on the state security side also be considered authorised officials or not, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, is it fair to say that not all employees of the MUP are authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But conversely, all authorised officials in the MUP are employees of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Can you give me some examples of MUP employees who would not be authorised officials? What type of personnel are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I think that category would include, for example, clerical employees, secretaries, stenographers. It would most likely also include or definitely include the canteen personnel, other people who are working and receive their salaries from the Ministry of Internal Affairs but who certainly don't have the -- either the right to carry fire-arms or to arrest individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to turn to your report, I'm going to generally try to go chronologically through some of the documents. And the first topic that I want to talk about deals with the separation or the fragmentation of the old BiH MUP. And the first document I want to show you is 65 ter number 038. This is tab 5 in your first binder. It's a 11 February 1992 meeting. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a meeting that was held in Banja Luka of, appears to be, senior officials of the MUP, and they all appear to be Serbians. Can you tell us about -- can you tell us about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: This meeting takes place, as can be seen, on the 11th of February 1992 in Banja Luka. As was stated, the people present are Serbs, ethnically, who are employees of the then Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina's Ministry of Internal Affairs, at various levels of that ministry. And in the document they -- which is basically the minutes of that meeting, they discuss their plans for the formation of a Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We note on page 1 that the first speaker listed is Stojan Zupljanin. And he is described as informing those present that a decision had been made that "not a single new Muslim or Croatian employee would be hired until the status of about 600 Serbian police employees from Croatia who had fled to BiH is resolved." Did you see any other reference in your review on documents about this situation and what might have happened concerning those former Serbian police employees from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Certainly it is the case that at this point there is an ongoing armed conflict on the territory of Croatia, and a number of ethnically Serb police officers who had up until that point been employed in Croatia fled to Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it was the position of many Bosnian Serbs in MUP in Bosnia and Herzegovina that these, as it were, refugee employees from the neighbouring Croatian MUP, who in most cases had arrived because they were discriminated against and had been fired by the Croatian MUP, should be able to find employment of some sort in Bosnian and Herzegovinian MUP. This was a point of contention as certainly I would say Bosnian Croat employees and some Bosnian Muslim employees disagreed with this solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And the second speaker is listed as Mico Stanisic is reported as saying: "The position of the council of ministers at the last session was that in the territories in SR BH which are under Serbian control, that control must be felt." Do you have the B/C/S there and can you tell us if you agree with that translation?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is an accurate translation in my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the council of ministers is referring to who or what, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: This is referring to the council of ministers that was established by the Serbian people, the Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were you aware that Mr. Stanisic was listed as a member of that council?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, and I note that in my report, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what do you understand this to mean, that control must be felt in the territories under Serbian control?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, control can be a very vague word, but I take it to mean that the authorities that are being established by the Serbian people in accordance with its Assembly during that period should be operational on the territory, that is, as he puts it, under Serbian control.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to turn to page -- page 2 in the English, page 3 in the B/C/S. Speaker listed is Predrag Jesuric. Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Predrag Jesuric is or was an official of MUP from Bijeljina in north eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He is noted as stating: "I did not receive any moral or material assistance from our MUP. I had to turn to the SR Serbia MUP, which was very helpful." Is that the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: It is the MUP of the then Socialist Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: And it accurately -- his statement accurately reflects the situation in which certain parts of the Ministry of Internal Affairs in which Serbian -- ethnic Serbian officers worked were at that point receiving material and other assistance from Belgrade from both the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Serbia and the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in your review of documents and in your report, I think you tell us about other examples of where the Serb MUP members received material assistance from the Republic of Serbia MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct, there is a section towards the end of my report that also focuses on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Both before and after the conflict began in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. He goes on to say: "I only trust my own people and weapons that I have acquired and hidden." Do you know why the MUP official would be hiding weapons, from whom, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: One could assume, based on other document, numerous other documents that refer to hiding of weapons, that the ethnic Serbian officials in the Bijeljina area were keeping those weapons that they had obtained, among other -- from among other sources from Belgrade hidden from their colleagues of other ethnicities. Certainly once we see retrospective reports being filed by the RS MUP about its functioning in 1991 and 1992, or that is to say more precisely, the functioning of Serbs in SR BiH MUP up to April 1992 and then the functioning of RS MUP after April 1992, they make retrospective references on a number of occasions to the quote unquote, illegal, collection of weapons and the -- even the illegal arming of ethnic Serbs in municipalities in which Bosnian Serbs were preponderant in the organs of Internal Affairs. I want to stress at this point because I will be using the term "illegal" on a number of occasions that whenever I do so, I'm not making any finding as an analyst about the illegality or legality of such actions; rather, I am merely noting that the original documents which were produced by Bosnian Serbs working for the organs of Internal Affairs themselves used that term. And I think as an analyst, that whether or not those actions were indeed illegal, it is highly salient and pertinent that they should choose to use that word. These are, after all, police officers and it is certainly my assumption that they themselves knew where the line was between legality and illegality at any specific point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. The next speaker is listed as Krsto Savic. Do you recall where he was from?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Krsto Savic is from eastern Herzegovina down in the Trebinje area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Later in 1992 became the head of the CSB in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At the bottom of page 2 in the English and page 4 of the B/C/S at the top, Savic says: "I would mention again that we are already establishing a SJB on the left side of the Neretva." This is February 11th. Were you aware of discussions that are sometimes referred to as the Lisbon talks or Lisbon conference, the Cutileiro agreement or the Cutileiro plan?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of those discussions, and for the sake of accuracy, I would note that it is neither an agreement nor a plan, but, rather, a set of principles that provides a framework for continued negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back to that in a little bit, but I want to finish with this document, by going to page 4 of the English and it's page 6 in the B/C/S. Under "Conclusions." Number 1 says: "A Serbian collegium is hereby established in the SR BH MUP, consisting of Serbian personnel at executive positions ..." can you tell me, in the regular MUP, the entire MUP, was there a collegium? Was that something provided for under the old Law on Internal Affairs or the old rule book for Internal Affairs that existed in early 1992 before the war began?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I have to say that I'm not aware whether what is here referred to in the English translation as "collegium" is specifically provided for in either the law of Internal Affairs from 1990 or the rule book that also stemmed from 1990. However, there certainly did exist such a body. Here it's translated as collegium. It's also something that in English we would refer to often as a senior staff meeting or senior staff steering council, and that, yes, such a body certainly existed and met, how frequently, I'm not sure, but certainly met at that point in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina's MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, are you aware of whether or not there was a Muslim collegium or a Croatian collegium established on or about this time?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I have not seen any specific references to such bodies. I have to say, given the situation in SR BiH MUP at the time, it would not surprise me if such bodies existed. Certainly, I believe that Bosnian Croats and Bosnian Muslims met on their own without Serbs being present to discuss certain issues, but here we see that it's a specific body that's being formed in the conclusions of this meeting, or not formed, but in fact, it seems to -- yes, being formed, excuse me, I misspoke, and that it is led by then assistant minister, Momcilo Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We see in item 2 that Momcilo Mandic has been named to manage the Serb collegium and ensure implementations of the decisions. Number 3 is that: "The collegium is instructed to carry out all preparations necessary for the functioning of the Serbian MUP after promulgation of the Serbian Republic of BH constitution." Do you know when the constitution was promulgated by the Bosnian Serbs, approximately?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I believe it was, I know that the Law on Internal Affairs comes into effect at this point on the 28th of February 1992. I have to admit that not being a political expert, I don't off the top of my hand - I'm not working with this issue every day - don't recall off the top of my head precisely when the constitution came into effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But there's no reference in this document about the functioning of the Serbian MUP waiting until something had been worked out with regard to the Cutileiro discussions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, point 3 simply states, I mean, taking the document at its word, that what needs to be waited for or needs to be awaited is the constitution of the Serbian Republic of BiH, not the -- not any international negotiations. There's no reference to such negotiations in that point of the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And item number 5 says: "Not a single decision regarding staffing policies in the SR BH MUP will be implemented without the approval of Momcilo Mandic." Now, who was the minister of Internal Affairs at this time in February 1992 of the MUP in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: The minister of Internal Affairs at that point in time was Alija Delimustafic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And to your understanding, according to the existing Law on Internal Affairs and the rule book, would Deputy Minister Mandic have some authority over and above Delimustafic concerning staffing policies?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: No, deputy -- well, I see that the transcript says "Deputy Minister Mandic," I want them to make it clear that we understand he's not a deputy minister, he's the assistant minister at this point in time. And no, he would not have had authority over Delimustafic, and he also was not primarily, he, Mandic, was not primarily responsible for staffing matters. However, I would say at a de facto level, it was certainly well known at this point in time in February, March, 1992 that it was Momcilo Mandic who was, to a considerable extent, the person that the Serbian Democratic Party looked to in resolving personnel issues affecting Serbian personnel in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to take you now to your report, paragraph 86. Begins at page 32 of English and goes on to page 33. There's a reference that I need some help and probably the Judges could use some help on understanding. You talk about some telephone conversation that Minister Mandic had where he was discussing what was happening with the MUP. And in one of those, you said Mandic spoke about showing Delimustafic and Zepinic who the real Boro and Ramiz were. Can you explain for us what that's a reference to? In March 1992, what do Boro and Ramiz refer to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Boro and Ramiz is a very well known Yugoslav cultural reference referring to the friendship of two persons of separate ethnicities, and it was to some extent a shorthand way of referring to a well functioning friendship or partnership among persons of different ethnicities precisely because of the Yugoslav system. So when Boro and Ramiz is referred to here in this paragraph, it's the notion that allegedly at that time in the public, and this is seen in some of the media sources, Delimustafic is the Ramiz, the Muslim, and Zepinic, Vitomir Zepinic is Boro, the Serb. And so their co-operation as minister, Delimustafic and Deputy Minister Zepinic, despite their different ethnicities was seen to embody this spirit of inter-ethnic co-operation, and here it's being referred to in a rather derisive way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, and I would next like to show you 65 ter number, well, I guess now it has an exhibit number, MFI, it's P353. This is tab 7 in your binder. It's a document dated the 31st of March. Are you familiar with this one?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is and what the significance of it was?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: The document we have before us is in many ways the birth certificate, one could say, of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is RS MUP. It is a document that is sent by the Assistant Minister Momcilo Mandic, to the minister of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to all municipal and regional offices of Internal Affairs in both public security and state security in Bosnian Herzegovina, and essentially announces the establishment of the Ministry of Internal Affairs in accordance with the new RS Law on Internal Affairs which will start functioning on 1st of April, 1992, that is to say, the following day. And as such, states that -- formally that the Bosnian Serbs are henceforth going to operate within the context of the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs in the context of their own Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have one question concerning the list of security service centres to be set up. The last one is listed as Ugljevik, pardon my pronunciation. Was there a Security Services Centre set up for the RS MUP in that location, and if not, can you tell us why?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: What actually transpires in the first half of April is that once the situation in Bijeljina becomes more stable from the Bosnian Serb point of view, they set up their Security Services Centre, the CSB, in Bijeljina. Ugljevik is a small town to the south of Bijeljina, and Mandic, at a later date, as I note in the report, sends out a dispatch stating that it should not be Ugljevik but rather Bijeljina that is the seat of the CSB in north eastern -- in the north eastern RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how would you describe the reaction, if any, to the sending of this dispatch on the 31st of March?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, the -- from the Bosnian Serb side the reaction is obviously to proceed as Mandic instructs. I don't have any immediate reaction from the Bosnian Croats, but I do have a reaction the same day from Minister Delimustafic, who on that day, and I believe it's tab -- maybe it's not in the binder here, but certainly in the report I refer to a dispatch from Delimustafic on the same day stating that Mandic's dispatch was illegal and that all subordinates in the ministry are to disregard the dispatch and proceed to function -- to continue to function as employees of a unified Bosnian and Herzegovinian Ministry of Internal Affairs. And Delimustafic in that dispatch also refers to his hope that despite a very grave security situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, they will nonetheless, as employees of Internal Affairs, be able to stabilise the situation and continue to operate as a unified ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If you could look at tab 8 in your binder, 65 ter number 1301. And I'll ask you if that's the --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- Delimustafic document that you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Pardon me, I skipped it by a tab. But, yes, that is precisely the dispatch I refer to, and as we can see it's sent out on the very same day, in fact around midday, by Delimustafic. He refers, as I said, to a very complex security situation. He refers to the dispatch giving the number of that dispatch and says that, from his perspective, this is null and void.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to look next at another document relating to this, it's tab 99 in your binder, which would be binder number 4 if you have all four. It's 65 ter number 326. This appears to be a dispatch sent also on the 31st of March from the Zvornik public security station. You find that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what can you tell us about that in connection with these dispatches on the 31st of March?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, here we see a reaction by a number of employees of the public security station in Zvornik on the same day, and they've obviously read both Mandic's dispatch and the subsequent dispatch, counter-dispatch as it were, by Alija Delimustafic, and it says that the employees of SJB Zvornik have decided to continue working in unison and to not divide on a national basis. It asks -- clearly they are confused. This is in Eastern Bosnia. They are very confused by the two contradictory dispatches they've received on that day, and they've therefore asked for further clarification and expressed the hope that the inter-ethnic conflict can be avoided. And they also state that they hope that everyone will continue to work as professionally and not on a political basis. And I would note that the list of names that appears at the bottom of both the English and the B/C/S is a list of names that are both Muslims and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move on to another topic, I wonder if this is an appropriate time for our first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, when I introduced you this morning, I failed to notify you of something which I should have done, namely the fact that for the purpose of your testimony here in this trial, the Stanisic Defence team has been reinforced by the Defence expert on MUP, Dr. Mladen Bajagic, who is sitting there in the middle, unrobed. So I just wanted to draw your attention to the fact that the gentleman sitting there is the Defence expert on the matters on which you will testify. Tom Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, I wanted to ask you about one thing in your report before I go to a discussion about Cutileiro. And it's at page 8, paragraph 4 where you talked about the aim of your report, and you indicated a reference to the November 1990 multi-party elections. You said: "These multi-party elections led directly to a multi-party agreement on the distribution of posts within the SR BiH MUP. This process in turn eventually contributed to the breakdown of the SR BiH MUP." Can you explain briefly how in your view that multi-party agreement on the distribution of posts within the MUP led to the breakdown of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Prior to the first multi-party elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina in November 1990, this had been a party state system in which the League of Communists was the sole political factor, and therefore also the sole factor behind various ministries and the staffing of ministries, as such. In the wake of the victory at the November 1990 elections of three, what I would term, nationally based or nationalist parties, the Serb Democratic Party, the Croat Democratic Union, and the Muslim Party of Democratic Action, they essentially divided posts in the Ministry of Internal Affairs in accordance with more or less the electoral results. I refer the Court to paragraph 7 of my report on page 10 in which I identify the party affiliation, as it were, of various ministers -- of the minister and various assistant ministers and deputy ministers in the MUP. I want to stress that just because a party affiliation appears in parentheses after their names, that does not denote that they were members of those parties. It rather notes that they were -- they enjoyed the support of those parties in holding that particular post in MUP between November 1990 and April 1992. While this original division of posts among the three parties was, as far as I've been able to tell, fairly uncontroversial, the continued jostling for position at all levels of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, micromanaging by political party leaders of who would in various political position -- police positions at the municipal and even village level, introduced an element in which it is clear that the support of a particular political party often overrode or certainly exceeded in importance the professional qualifications of those candidates being considered for that position in the police. And I've seen references by Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, and by Bosnian Serbs in the police who deplore what they perceive to be a politicisation and increasingly acrimonious one of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. So that's what I mean when I say that it contributed to a generally deteriorating situation in which political affiliation and support, rather than professionalism, became a guiding factor in choosing personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the general impact of that on the professionalism of the MUP was what?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, certainly it's a factor of functioning states that the civil service, the state apparatus, of which the police is a part, is held to be outside of party politics to the degree in SR BiH MUP that this was no longer the case and to the degree that every single appointment became the point of contention on a national or ethnic basis, then certainly it meant that over the long term, certain persons who arguably should not have been appointed to positions of authority in the police did, in fact, receive such appointments, and that had a negative effect on the professionalism of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I take it that that's not just your view, you saw that view expressed by police professionals of all three ethnicities in the documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. And I would point out that in the document we viewed prior to the break from SJB Zvornik, there we see employees of both Bosnian, Muslim, and Serbian ethnicity expressing regret that things are being resolved on a mono-national basis rather than on a professional basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to follow up on our discussion about the break-up of the Bosnian Herzegovina MUP by directing you to first of all tab 84.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 3452.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a document entitled: "Statement of Principles for New Constitutional Arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina." Have you seen that before today?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I was shown this document last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you're familiar with what it concerns?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tell me, if you could, what these principles are about and what they are related to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry Your Honours, I just lost the LiveNote on my computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So did I.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Me too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand there's a technical problem which should be corrected in five minutes, so we'll just wait. If it's longer than that, we'll have to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand from the technicians that the problem is now solved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me re-ask the question, Doctor. Could you tell me what those principles are about and what they are related to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: As I understand this document, this reflects a statement of principles for a possible new constitutional arrangement for Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is from, I believe, the 15th -- no, the 18th of March, 1992, as is reflected on the final page of the document, and it states very clearly in capital letters immediately above the date that this paper is the basis of further negotiations, so that is the context in which I made my earlier statement that this is not a plan or an agreement, but rather a framework for continued negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. In your binder at tabs 85 through 98, and these are 65 ter numbers 3453 through 3466, I don't want to bring all those up right now, but do you recall having a chance to look through all of those documents before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: They appear to be primarily correspondence to and maybe one or two from Mr. Cutileiro with Bosnian Serb leaders, Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there's been some suggestion in the trial to date in questioning of witnesses that the division of the Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP and the creation of a separate Serbian MUP was simply being done pursuant to Cutileiro agreement or Cutileiro plan. Based on your review of the documents, did you see anything to support that, or to refute it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: It is my view based on my review of these documents last week and based on the review of the documents that are cited in my report and that were previously cited in my report, that the division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in -- at the beginning of April 1992, certainly took place simultaneously with ongoing, and I stress the word "ongoing" negotiations, about the future constitutional arrangement of Bosnia and Herzegovina as is reflected in the principles document. These negotiations presupposed a sovereign state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they did envisage that policing, and this is reflected in section D of the document, of the principles document, would take place henceforth at the level of the constituent units that might - and again I stress the word "might" - be formed within Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, this was not a final agreement, it was not a final plan. I'm aware of the fact that Alija Izetbegovic, in his capacity as the head of the SDA, withdrew his signature in late March from this document. I'm also aware of the fact that on the day Momcilo Mandic sent his dispatch establishing RS MUP, there were negotiations in Brussels at which the SDS leadership and the SDA leadership were present but that it did not reach a definitive agreement on this point, and I think this is actually to some extent reflected in Mandic's dispatch, and further dispatches of other officials within RS MUP, which refer to a possible future state organisation; that is, there is a large element of contingency remaining, and as such, I do not believe that the formation of RS MUP can be said to have taken place on the basis of a trilateral final agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see in your review of the documents any contemporaneous assertions in the MUP documents that suggested that the creation of a separate Serbian MUP was being done pursuant to the Lisbon talks or Cutileiro?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Certainly if we could go back to the 31st March 1992 dispatch, perhaps I could be told what tab number that was?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry, that is tab number 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's Exhibit P353 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, that's Exhibit P353 MFI. It's tab 7 in your binder, if you are talking about Mr. Mandic's dispatch.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's the dispatch to which I referred. In this dispatch, as I noted in my previous response, he says that this decision to form a separate Ministry of Internal Affairs is in accordance with the decision of the Assembly of the Serbian people, and, I believe, he also refers to the quote unquote, Sarajevo agreement, thus the gist of Mandic's dispatch is certainly to make it appear as if this decision is talking place based on some agreement with the other parties. However, if that were the case, it certainly does not explain why Delimustafic would then react so promptly by responding and accusing Mandic of doing something that is illegal and inappropriate. I would also note that I have reviewed other documents stemming from later in 1992, in which Mandic and also Tomislav Kovac who became a leading figure in the RS MUP, refer in quite different tones to the establishment of the ministry, or more appropriately, the closing down of SR BiH MUP. There in those documents that I've reviewed, they refer to the end of SR BiH MUP in terms that leave no doubt that this was not done based on an agreement, but it was rather an attempt, as Tomislav Kovac expressed it, to destroy SR BiH MUP. Mandic on 5 May, 1992, uses a quite profane term in B/C/S to say that the Bosnian Serbs basically of their own volition and without any agreement dissolved SR BiH MUP and that it was a unilateral decision to form RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that last reference to Mr. Mandic, you are referring to a telephone conversation that's referred to in 65 ter number 1097, I believe it's tab 18 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we are coming to the intercept issue. We objected to it and, therefore, we renew our objection on all intercepts that are to be used in this case, including this one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, are you seeking to have document 1097 admitted into evidence, or are you just touching briefly upon the telephone intercepts for the purposes of testimony? Where are we going?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm intending to do the most I'm permitted to do today, but it is a part of his report. I know with some of our prior witnesses intercepts have been part of 92 ter packages for some of those witnesses. We have some intercepts in that way. This intercept is a footnoted document in his report. If -- if it's is problem at this juncture, I can ask him another question and we can deal with it later. But there are some intercepted conversations which are footnoted documents in his report which are on our 65 ter list and which we will be seeking to admit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The Chamber expects to the issue the decision on the intercepts tomorrow hopefully, or certainly before the recess, so I would prefer if at this moment you could just, you know, put another question to the witness so as to avoid the uncertainty about the status of the intercepts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I can do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, are you aware of any comments by Mr. Mandic after March 31st, 1992, for example, in a media interview where he described his role in connection with that dispatch, and the effect it had on the then existing MUP in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am. If I could just be permitted a few seconds to find that because I would prefer to quote it directly. It's, I believe, footnote 145 in paragraph 94 of my report, that's on page 35 of the report. In 1998, Momcilo Mandic was interviewed by the Bosnian news magazine "Slobodna Bosna" and in that interview referring not specifically, I must note, to the 31st March dispatch, but to the establishment of the RS MUP's headquarters at the contested school of Internal Affairs at Vraca right outside Sarajevo, Mandic said that, and I quote: "When we set out for Vraca to take the police academy, we knew that we would be shot dead as terrorists if we failed. We knew that BH, that is Bosnia-Herzegovina, would be recognised on 7 April. If I and Karisik Special Police had not raided, we would certainly have been proclaimed terrorists and the BH state would have executed us." This certainly seems to suggest from Momcilo Mandic's perspective, that there was not an agreement to separate the school of Internal Affairs to divide it, and by extension that there was no agreement to form a separate Ministry of Internal Affairs. However, I want to stress again that my conclusion as an analyst here on the absence of an agreement is not based on any one document, but is in fact based cumulatively on a review of considerable amount of documents first and foremost Delimustafic's counter -- order countermanding Mandic's dispatch on the 31st of March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regard to your review of the documents and timing vis-a-vis Cutileiro discussions, did you see evidence of planning for a separate Serbian MUP prior to Mr. Cutileiro ever appearing on the scene?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: There are a large number of documents which refer to such planning, to advance stages of both contemplation and action aimed towards the establishment of a separate Ministry of Internal Affairs based on ethnicity, and in this case particularly RS MUP. The draft 1992 annual report of RS MUP, which I refer to towards the end of my report on pages 107 to 109, is among the seminal documents produced by RS MUP itself, which retrospectively refer to, again their word, illegal actions taken to plan for and establish a separate Ministry of Internal Affairs, independent of any negotiations that were ongoing in the spring of 1992. So, yes, certainly there were planning -- there was planning for a separate Serbian MUP as early, I think, as September and October of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, are you aware of a specific statement made by Radovan Karadzic to the RS Assembly in 1994 concerning Cutileiro?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that Karadzic made statements at a later date, the gist of which - and I don't have the statement fresh if my head - but the gist of which is certainly that there was not an agreement, and, in fact, I'm also aware of subsequent documentation stemming from Cutileiro himself, which certainly suggests that he wanted to have negotiations ongoing, even after the beginning of armed conflict on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that he did not himself view any negotiations over which he had presided in resulting in a tripartite agreement on the division of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move to another topic. You talk in your report about the RS or the Serbian Republic of BiH Law on Internal Affairs. It's tab 6 in your binder. That's 65 ter number 053. And you discuss this report at some -- this law at some length in your report. This law was first passed by the Bosnian Serb Assembly or the Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina on 28 February 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That's correct. And if I may be permitted, that is in fact the same day that the Assembly adopted the constitution. I was able to refresh my memory on that point by looking at my own report during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraph 98 of your report, page 36 of the English, you mentioned two points that you wanted to note in comparing the new Law on Internal Affairs with the pre-existing law. The first point was that there's a very large overlap in the wording between those two; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the other point you wanted to make, that this is a relatively small document compared to the rule book for Internal Affairs, which has a lot more detail about the specific regulations controlling the workings and internal relationships of members of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. Both prior to 1992 and the formation of RS MUP and after the formation of RS MUP and, in fact, until the present day, there are a number of legal instruments that are germane to the functioning of the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the RS. The law is, of course, the basic document governing Internal Affairs in the RS. However, the much longer, in the 1992 version, it was approximately 200 pages long, rule book on the internal organisation of RS MUP sets out in exhaustive detail what everyone in the ministry does from the minister down to the janitorial personnel. And in both cases, the case of the Law on Internal Affairs, as well as the case of the rule book, the 1990 SR BiH MUP documents on those subjects were very much the model used by the officials forming the RS MUP, as I think is in fact quite natural for them to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraph 98 you point out some of the distinctions in terminology, and I think that the three that are primarily important for us to be aware of concern the difference between the old law which referred to the "republican secretariat" and the "secretary" as opposed to the new law which uses the term "ministry" and "minister." That's one; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the term "working people" is replaced in the -- replaces the the term "citizens" from the old law?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. And both changes reflect the types of legal changes which were taking place throughout eastern Europe at this time as these countries made transitions from socialist party states to multi-party systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the last one that I think we need to be aware of is the old law referred to "state security," and the new law, the term is "national security" for referring to the side of the MUP that deals with matters regarding the security of the entity; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. From April 1992 until the end of 1993, the RS MUP used the term "national security" rather than "state security." At that point in 1994, they reverted to the more traditional term "state security."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just a few of the changes I want to ask you about. The first one is at page 39 of your report in paragraph 113.
