You point out that in Article 22 of the old law, the 1990 law, there was a requirement for the secretariat to report to -- not only the appropriate republican organs, but also the federal organ, that is -- that would have been the Republic of Yugoslavia, correct, I guess the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the new law also contained that language even though the new republic, the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or as it later was called the Republika Srpska, was an independent country and a separate part not in Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, the Republika Srpska was not a part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Serbia and Montenegro after April/May of 1992, but this language seems to allow them to continue to report to Belgrade on matters that are relevant for security of the country. I think in practice it's certainly the case, as I note in my report, that there are documentary illustrations of continued communication between the officials of RS MUP and their counter-parts in MUP of Serbia and in the Federal Secretariat of Internal Affairs in Belgrade. One illustration of this is the fact that when the top officials of RS MUP have a meeting to discuss the entire situation that the ministry is confronting in the field and in the seat of the ministry itself, and that is a meeting that takes place on the 11th of July, 1992, they, in fact, meet in Belgrade in Serbia, not in the RS, and that the minutes prepared from that meeting, and which are cited in my report, reflect that a leading official of the Federal Secretariat for Internal Affairs is in fact also present during that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Article 28, in the old law there were nine CSBs listed. Under the new law in the -- what becomes the Republika Srpska there are five CSBs. And I guess that's a reflection of the fact that the RS is a smaller territory than the former BiH?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I think it would also be an appropriate place to note that there is a new place for a CSB, namely CSB Trebinje. Previously Trebinje had been a subordinate to CSB Mostar, and it was, in fact, a long-running wish of the Bosnian Serbs expressed in numerous documents that there be a separate CSB established in Trebinje, and they certainly did that once they had their own ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the CSB in Bijeljina in the new law appears to be a new CSB as well?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that would previously have been subordinate, I believe, to Tuzla, and again, as we discussed earlier this morning, this is in Bijeljina and not in Ugljevik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, we saw that in Mr. Mandic's dispatch on the 31st of March. This law was passed on the 28th of February; correct? Do you know why Mr. Mandic's dispatch had Ugljevik instead of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: It's a matter that I looked into a number of years ago, but that, quite frankly, I am not in a position right now with certainty to comment on. As I stated earlier, it may have had something to do with the fact that the situation in Bijeljina was not from the Bosnian Serb point of view stable at the time that the law was passed, but that is speculation on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware of the date that Arkan and his men helped take part in the take-over of power in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I believe that it is a well-known fact, and in fact reflected in trial and appeal judgements from this Tribunal, that Arkan and his paramilitary forces entered Bijeljina and established control over that municipality at the very beginning of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next section I want to ask you about is at page 45 of the English. It's paragraph 150 in your report. And it refers to Article 102 of the old 1990 law, which read in part as follows: "Workers of the republican secretariat may not engage in activities that are incompatible with their duty. A republican secretary will determine which activities are affected by the previous paragraph." That provision was not incorporated in the new law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that there was some controversy about that provision in the 1990 law prior to the creation of the new law at the end of February 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that and I, in some detail, explore a little bit of that controversy in footnote 163 on page 45. This relates to the transition of which I spoke a bit earlier; namely, the transition from a party state to a multi-party system. And we see uncertainty and indecision on the part of several factors that are involved in the drafting of Internal Affairs laws in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the 1990 to 1992 period as to whether particularly political activities of professional police officers should be permitted or forbidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in your footnote 163, and you make reference to a draft law proposing to change Article 102 to have some specific prohibitions in connection with authorised officials taking part in political functions or holding political office, or being guided by their political convictions in carrying out their task, or expressing or advocating those political views; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. However, as I state in the final sentence of that footnote, there is no indication that that draft law was, in fact, adopted, or that it affected the 1992 RS Law on Internal Affairs since that it was in such language as not to be found in the 1992 law.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And related to this article, I think it's Article 114 of the old law, there was a list of 12 separate kinds of conduct which were described as being misconduct for purposes of the law. And in the old law there was a clause 12 which prohibited involvement in activities incompatible with official duties; basically, the language of Article 102, correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. And as I state, in the report, both the article of the 1992 law as well as -- excuse me, of the 1990 law, Article 102 and clause 12 of article -- of the relevant article of the 1990 law are not present in the corresponding article in the 1992 law. In other words, any prohibitions in the Law on Internal Affairs on conducting activities that are allegedly incompatible with official duty are excised from the 1990 -- 1992 RS MUP law. I wish to also, in light of my prior testimony in Krajisnik, and having reviewed this report in the mean time, state that this was raised in the Krajisnik trial, and I stand by my interpretation of the law as it is in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And given the nature of police appointments that were being made to the MUP in early 1992, would that provision have any bearing on individuals named as police chiefs, et cetera, in the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, I am aware of the fact from reading the Assembly minutes of the Assembly of the Serbian nation that throughout 1992 there was a very lively discussion ongoing about the extent to which the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party, should exercise control of the police and the extent to which party bodies, such as the Crisis Staffs established by the SDS, could intervene in the police up to and including appointing chiefs of, for example, public security stations. So in this context, there is, one could say, very little to hinder police officials from actively engaging in political activity whether for the SDS or, for that matter, other political parties. Certainly, if we look at the period prior to 1992 and prior to April 1992, then I think in light of the party political distribution of leading posts in SR BiH MUP, the politicisation, as I said earlier this morning, of the police suited not just the SDS, but to a significant extent the HDZ and the SDA and, as such, that probably is one of the main reasons why the draft amendment of the law, which would in fact have inserted a prohibition against political activity of professional police officers was never in fact enacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I want to turn to some documents that deal with the organisation and structure and reporting within the -- within the RS MUP. The first document I'd like to look at is at tab 11 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's 65 ter number 1858. This is a document dated the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you'll see that the preface says: "According to the Law on Internal Affairs, I hereby issue the following order:" This has a signature and a stamp apparently from the Minister Mico Stanisic, and item 2 is to the TO staffs in the area of the Serb autonomous district of Romanija. It says: "They shall form a commission to take an inventory of materiel and technical equipment of the barracks in Falitici [phoen]. The inventory lists are to be sent to the MUP not later than 18 April." Can you tell me. Can you tell me where in the law Mr. Stanisic, as minister of the interior, has the authority to issue an order to the TO staffs, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, Mico Stanisic as the minister of Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina does not have, in the Law on Internal Affairs, a direct authority to order the TO, that is the Territorial Defence units, or its members, to perform any actions. It seems if one takes the whole context of this particular document, that he is doing so on the basis of an earlier agreement in which the police was supposed to obtain some equipment that seems to have been removed by someone else, and he seeks to rectify that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And paragraph 4 indicates any individual who fails to act on this order shall be arrested and placed in custody. That suggested he appears to believe he has the authority to do that, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: In any case in which I see a minister of Internal Affairs, whoever that person might be, issuing orders, then certainly I would go so far as to say at that point in time that minister certainly seems to think that he has the authority to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next one I would like to look at is Exhibit 1D46 in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You'll find it at tab 22, Doctor. You see it's dated the 15th of May. Again the preface says: "Pursuant to the Law on Internal Affairs, I hereby order:" It is signed and stamped apparently by Mico Stanisic, and this is a document you talk about in your report where he is establishing war units within the MUP. Concerning the date, do you recall the date in which the VRS, the Republika Srpska Army was formed in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I believe that was on the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in paragraph 7, which is at page 2 of the English, and I am not sure if it's on page 2 of the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. "The use of ministry units in co-ordinated action with the armed forces of the Serbian Republic of BH may be ordered by the minister of the interior, commander of the police detachment of the ministry, and chief of the CSB." In that context, do you know what the reference to armed forces of the Serbian Republic of BH refers to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: As I'm quite certain I state in the report, after the formation of the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska, on the 12th of May, 1992, and henceforth, the term "armed forces" includes in this case also the police, but in particular here it's referring to the co-operation between the units of the ministry with the army and the remaining TO forces, which are at that point being subsumed by the Ministry of Defence, and that is the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The third paragraph under number 7 says: "While participating in combat operations, the units of the ministry shall be subordinated to the command of the armed forces. However, the ministry units shall be under the direct command of certain ministry officials." What do you understand that to mean about control over the MUP units engaged in combat with the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Certainly, it's the case throughout the period from April 1992 until the end of 1992 that there are combat activities in which units of RS MUP participate. The draft 1992 annual report notes extremely extensive involvement of RS MUP units in combat activities. The way I read this is as saying that when these RS MUP units are in the field involved in combat activities, then they are subordinate to VRS command, but that in doing so the ranking official on the MUP side, whatever his rank may be at that point in time, will continue to directly command the employees of the ministry. If we are to take an abstract example, this would mean that if a unit of the police is out in the field and they are subordinated to a VRS colonel or major, then that colonel or major would issue orders to the police in the context of their joint combat activities, but he would do so by going through the relevant police commander who is the ranking police commander on the field. Bureaucratically speaking this is a quite predictable assertion of the jurisdiction and separateness of the police, even in the context of joint military activities. They participate in such activities, but they retain their status as police and are to be commanded through the ranking police officials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, what do you mean by "bureaucratically speaking"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what I mean by that, looking at it as a historian, is that the minister in most ministries, in most countries, even when there are joint activities taking place that involve employees of several ministries at the same time is going to make sure that ultimately at the end of day, so to speak, his employees still report back to him, and that they cannot, for any longer period of time, be used to carry out activities without his consent. And as we see later in the same order, in fact, and in subsequent dispatches from RS MUP, it's clear that if the RS MUP officials or employees were involved in combat activities, this was not a carte blanche that was being issued to the Ministry of Defence, but that the Ministry of Internal Affairs and its leadership expected to be informed on a rolling basis about their use in any additional actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But that would depend on the conditions for the resubordination, would it not, and are you able to testify about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether I'm -- is the question, Your Honour, am I able to testify on the question of resubordination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, because I certainly understand your that from -- as you call it, from a bureaucratic point of view, any minister would expect exactly what you have told us, but my intervention was based on the observation that there might be other considerations, meaning other than bureaucratic considerations, to determine the exercise of control over police units that have been resubordinated to the army. And that's why I'm saying, or suggesting to you that what from a bureaucratic point of view may seem obvious, may not be so obvious if you see it from a military point of view. But I'm just putting a question to the -- to you in this in order to clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I am, of course, aware that this Trial Chamber will hear testimony from a military expert, and I defer to him on questions of a specifically military nature. Obviously, and I'm certainly not the only case of this, when we have experts who testify, one on the police, and one on the military, there will always be a question of where one person's expertise ends and the other person's begins. What I am commenting on here is based on my reading of police documents and a number of military documents in which joint military activities are discussed, and in the specific case the 15 May order that we have in front of us. I think the most appropriate thing to do in -- as regards point 7 that we have in front of us, is to say that my reading of it is that even though units of the ministry are subordinate to the command of the armed forces, they are being directly commanded during those activities by certain ministry officials or employees, and that is just simply reading what point 7 says. I can -- will point out, and it's pointed out and dealt with at length in the report, that from the minister himself down to the municipal officials in the police throughout 1992, there was considerable resentment at the fact that the police were overwhelmingly engaged in combat activities during that year, and therefore were not available to do their jobs, as it were, which is to perform the tasks of Internal Affairs. I see this as a bureaucratic attempt to limit the extent to which employees of Internal Affairs can be seconded and ordered by the Ministry of Defence and its officials in the army, specifically because they have to do so through the direct command, as it says, of certain employees of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in item number 9 we see that the order establishes a staff to command and control the overall forces of the ministry. And it lists that Mr. Stanisic, the minister of the interior, will be the commander, listed deputy commander, and members to include the chiefs and the CSBs and the commander of the police detachment, among others. Could you look next at, in your binder, the tabs 23 through 28, reflect appointments following on this order. Tab 24 is 65 ter -- I'm sorry, tab 23 is 65 ter 1494. And we see that that is the appointment of Mico Stanisic as commander, and that appointment is made by Mico Stanisic the minister; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next one, two, three, four -- five documents, 65 ter numbers 2368 through 2372, that's tabs 24 through 28 in your binder, reflect appointments on the same day, 15th May of four CSBs chiefs, including Mr. Zupljanin, as well as the appointment of Milenko Karisik to this staff that we just saw in the previous order; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And all those appointments are made by the minister, Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, they are all made and they are made on the same day in which he issues the order that we were looking at previously, on the 15th of May 1992, the day that the staff is established.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me move to a different order addressed to a different addressee. This is tab number 33 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it is Exhibit P377, which has previously been marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's a very short order dated the 29th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I think I've got the wrong document up in e-court. I may have transposed my digits. I'm looking for a 26 June 1992 document. I have it as 377 MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 337, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, we are a minute shy of the break, do you want to take the break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This would be a good time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just in terms of scheduling, I'm advised, Mr. Zecevic, that I hope to finish with my direct of this witness by the end of the day, if all goes well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, the exhibit I did want to show you is Exhibit P337 marked for identification. And it's on the screen now. It is at tab 33 in your binder dated 29 June, 1992. And it appears to be an order from the minister of the interior, Mico Stanisic, to the Zvornik public security station asking or directing that they allow a certain confiscated Golf vehicle to be used by the Kalesija SJB. My question is did you see other documents where the minister is writing directly to a public security station rather than going through one of the CSBs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Normally, if it the minister of Internal Affairs is directing something to be done at the municipal level, whatever that might be, he would be issuing that time of instruction through the regional CSBs, the Security Services Centres. He is, of course, not prohibited from going straight to the SJB and ordering them to do something. I would, however, note looking now at the signature on this page, that despite the fact that the English translation says that it's signed and stamped and it says -- like, I think there's even a spelling mistake there, it says "Tanisic," it's obviously "Stanisic," but the original says in print "minister for Internal Affairs, Mico Stanisic," but as is sometimes the case one can see that someone has signed for him, and the signature -- certainly if we compare the signature to that present on the 15 May appointments that we reviewed earlier today is not the minister's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And based on your review of documents, is it a signature that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Not immediately, I must say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Do you recall seeing other documents from the minister directly to an SJB and not being copied to a CSB or an administration with -- oh, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, just to make sure, in the transcript this is referred to as 337. I couldn't find it on your list. Would that be 377?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I had incorrectly numbered it on my list, 377.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And I didn't correct that yet, sorry about that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Dr. Nielsen, do you recall seeing other documents directly from the minister of interior to an SJB not copied to the CSB or other administrations within the MUP headquarters, or do you recall?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I don't immediately recall seeing other such documents. What clearly is the pattern in the overwhelming majority of documents is that orders going to the SJBs went through the CSBs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document I want to discuss is tab 36 in your binder, it's 65 ter number 176, which I believe has Exhibit P427.8. It's a 17 July 1992 report on some aspects of the work done to date and the task ahead. And if we can go to page 2 -- well, before we do, you see that's addressed to the Presidency and the prime minister -- the president of the Presidency and the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: The handwriting on the first page of the original B/C/S document states that it was provided to the Presidency -- president of the Presidency and the president of the government. That is what we normally would call the prime minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And on page 2 at the beginning we see that the minister of the interior then called a meeting -- held a meeting in Belgrade on 11 July 1992. Have you seen and reviewed the minutes of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I referred to that document earlier today and it is cited the 11 July 1992 minutes are cited in the report several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in this document, I'd like to go to page 3 of the English, page 4 of the B/C/S. Top of the English page and, I think, top of the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The first paragraph says: "The army, Crisis Staffs, and War Presidencies have requested that the army round up or capture as many Muslim civilians as possible, and they leave such undefined camps to Internal Affairs organs. The conditions in some of these camps are poor: There is no food, individuals sometimes do not observe international norms, et cetera." Did you see -- besides your review of the meeting of 11 July 1992, prior to this date had you seen MUP documents referring to this phenomena of as many Muslim civilians as possible being rounded up or captured and put into undefined camps?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I've seen a large and reviewed a large number of RS MUP documents that refer to numerous civilians of Bosnian Muslim ethnicity being, as it were, detained and then subsequently held in a number of facilities, among those facilities were facilities that were controlled by the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in those documents often times you see MUP employees complaining about MUP personnel being tasked to guard the detainees in those facilities; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have reviewed such documents. The MUP personnel guard the detainees in a number of those facilities, and the MUP personnel are also on numerous occasions conducting investigations or, they say informational interviews or conversations with the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And those detainees were prisoners of war, civilians, both?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: There are a number of indications in the documents produced by RS MUP itself throughout the summer of 1992 that they made efforts to come up with a categorisation of detainees. The initial reason offered by the RS MUP for their detention is usually the failure from the RS MUP's point of view of those individuals to surrender weaponry that they allegedly possessed. It should be stated that in a number of cases, quite a large number of cases, the RS MUP itself was not the detaining organ, rather these people were detained in many cases by the VRS. And, in fact, the RS MUP often -- as indeed at this meeting, speaks of the large number of people that have been rounded up by the VRS and put in facilities controlled by the MUP as a problem. As they evolved their thinking in the summer of 1992, the officials of the RS MUP, as I said, develop a categorisation of these prisoners, the vast majority of whom are eventually lumped in a category in which it appears from the RS MUP's documentation that they themselves have reached the conclusion that these are not prisoners of war and that there is no substantial evidence linking them to hostile activity, and they are then through the offices of among other things, the International Red Cross, allowed to leave these facilities and eventually leave the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I deal with this in quite some length in my report in the section from pages 81 to page 90, and there I offer up a large selection of documents that substantiate the comments that I just made.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In that connection, in fairness isn't it correct that sometimes the MUP -- some MUP employees are also complaining about the conditions in which these people are being held, and the fact that some of them are civilians apparently being held without any criminal charges being filed against them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, the documents I reviewed do indeed reflect such concerns, sometimes uttered by employees of RS MUP themselves, sometimes written into reports filed by, for example, the VRS, but in which they deal with prisoners who have been held in facilities such as Omarska in Prijedor municipality which was under the control of the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Based on your review of the documents however, is the more common complaint about the fact that the MUP is being required to guard these people rather than the other matters we just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I want it to make it very clear that both complaints are frequently uttered. However, it is the case that the -- and this is obviously a qualitative statement based on the reading of a large number of documents, that the primary concern of RS MUP from the SJB level up to the leading officials of the ministry -- for example, the officials who participate in the 11 July 1991 [sic] meeting, seems to be with the inordinate amount of man-hours and resources that RS MUP is, from their perspective, losing because they have to guard a substantial number of detention facilities in which a very considerable number of people are being detained. The frequency with which RS MUP complains in its own internal reports about the drain of resources on the ministry which such detention facilities represent, is to a large extent analogous to the complaints that the ministry officials also have about the extensive involvement of RS MUP officials in combat activities during the same period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, if we could stay on page 3 of the English and go to page --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just intervention in transcript 62, 20, I believe the document refers to 11 July 1992 and that is what I believe the witness have said. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, would you agree the meeting on 11 July was July 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is of course correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, staying on page 3 in the English going to page 5 in the B/C/S, the last paragraph, it's referring to the minister who is pointing out that the government is preparing a new political and territorial division of the Serbian republic which will replace the previously necessary forms such as autonomous Serb areas and regions with districts. This will require the MUP to adjust to the re-organisation. Do you know what the organisational structure of the MUP was in the relation to the Serb autonomous regions; for example, vis-a-vis CSBs, the Security Services Centres, were they aligned with the Serb autonomous regions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I think in discussing the RS MUP and the Serb autonomous regions or SAOs, I've been able to distinguish several phases in their relationship. During the second half of 1991, and I believe the first SAOs were formed in September 1991, we see a growing co-ordination between Bosnian Serb employees in various regions of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the RS MUP -- or excuse me, in the SR BH MUP with the organs that are being formed of these Serb autonomous regions. This co-ordination is increasing until the beginning of the war in April 1992. From approximately April 1992 until this meeting in July, there are numerous instances in which the police are closely co-ordinating their activities with the organs of the still existing autonomous regions in the RS. However, by - and it is expressed in this document and other documents from the summer of 1992 - by the summer of 1992, from the RS MUP's perspective and from the minister's perspective, there is a need to consolidate decision-making on a variety of issues strictly within the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and in such a way that the RS MUP starts to disassociate itself from the Serb autonomous areas and these Serb autonomous areas are, of course, also eventually closed down during the course of the second half of 1992. But from the first quarter of RS MUP's existence, it is the case that you see a close co-ordination in many fields between the SAO leaderships and the chiefs of the CSBs in areas such as Trebinje, Banja Luka, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Relating to that I have a question about the assignment of SJBs to particular CSBs and, in particular, I want to ask you about Doboj. You are aware that there was quite a controversy about whether Teslic municipality and Teslic SJB were going to be affiliated with other -- the ARK and Banja Luka CSB or with Doboj?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that that particular SJB was contested within the RS MUP, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And at the beginning of the conflict in April 1992, Teslic was assigned or connected with CSB in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who had the authority to make the decision about which CSB a SJB would be reporting to or subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, certainly prior to 1992, it was usually set out in the laws referring to the ministry, and it would be clearly delineated particularly in the rule book also where these SJBs would be subordinate to. It's quite unusual, in fact I think the case of Teslic is unique, that you see an internal struggle or contestation within the RS MUP about the placement of a certain SJB with respect to its CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. Let me turn next to page 6 of the English and page 11 of the B/C/S. And the middle of the page in English and the B/C/S I think. Paragraph begins: "To resolve the observed problems and the dispute over jurisdiction between the MUP and the army, a joint meeting should be prepared to address all of the problems in order to reach an agreement..." Going on the next sentence begins: "Special emphasis should be placed on: The activity of paramilitary formations, the problem of engaging police in combat activities when not necessary, the co-ordinated efforts of the army and MUP to prevent crime, and the procedure and jurisdiction with regard to the treatment and holding of prisoners, among others." Are you aware of what the problem or dispute about jurisdiction between the MUP and the army was in relation to the activity of paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, I am aware that during the summer of 1992, orders were issued by President Radovan Karadzic that were then reiterated in orders of the VRS stating that paramilitary formations needed to be disbanded and that to the extent, I believe, the language, and I'm para-phrasing here, but I believe that to the extent that these groups, these paramilitary formations were engaged in activities that were positive from the perspective of the Serbian nation, they should be integrated into the Army of Republika Srpska. There were a number of cases in various municipalities and regions of the RS throughout the summer of 1992 in which it proved quite difficult to in fact carry out that order. Paramilitary formations remained active in a number of geographical areas in the RS. And on occasion there were conflicts between the police and the army about who was doing what to implement that order. So I think the way this is read or this is to be read in this particular point of this document is that they realised that to avoid any unnecessary conflict and given that they are ostensibly working towards the same goal, they need to co-ordinate better and to make sure that they get these paramilitary formations disbanded as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, if paramilitary individual or formation was observed committing a crime against civilians, for example, who had the jurisdiction or authority to detain and/or arrest and process those individuals, was it the MUP, was it the army, was it both or some combination?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I deal with in my report with the case of the Yellow Wasps as they were called, a paramilitary formation that was quite active in Zvornik municipality, and which represented from the perspective of the RS authorities a serious danger to the stability of the legitimate authorities of the RS in that municipality. And because of that concern, the special unit or special detachment as it was called, of the police, of the RS MUP, actually in an operation in which some military police officers were involved as well, moved decisively at the end of July 1992 to remove the Yellow Wasps from the streets of Zvornik, as it were. The documents which I was able to find and review in RS MUP reveal that the -- certainly for the individuals that the MUP arrested during that operation, it was the MUP that was in charge of the initial detention and processing of those individuals and as would happen, with arrests of individuals by the MUP, once they had been detained and arrested, it was up to the judicial organs to further determine the nature of the investigation of such individuals. I don't know what would have happened precisely with those paramilitary formations who were detained or arrested by the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware the involvement of any individuals or unit from the federal SUP in the Yellow Wasp operation?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I know from the documents that I reviewed that there was co-ordination with the authorities of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, as it was called at that point in time, and this because Zvornik is a municipality that borders the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and for that reason it was quite natural and necessary to co-ordinate this particular effort with officials of the neighbouring state.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. On this document, my last question, it mentions procedure and jurisdiction with regard to the treatment and holding of prisoners. Do you know what prior to this was the nature of the observed problems and dispute over jurisdiction between the MUP and the army about that issue of treatment and holding of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: This involved a number of issues. One was the disputed responsibility for guarding some facilities. There are documents that one sees from Prijedor municipality in which there seems to be an effort by the police to divest itself of responsibility for guarding facilities and to handover these facilities to the army, or alternately, in some cases in which police officials had been seconded and were guarding facilities that were formerly detention centres under the control of the army, there was again a wish from the perspective of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the RS to have the army overtake full responsibility for the guarding of those facilities, and therefore to free up the scarce resources of the RS MUP personnel so that they could be involved in other activities. Later, particularly in August 1992, as a number of detention facilities, particularly in northwestern Bosnia-Herzegovina on the territory of what was called the Autonomous Region of Krajina, were dismantled pursuant to international pressure once the conditions in those facilities became a matter of public knowledge, one sees a number of very tense disagreements between MUP personnel and VRS officers. The MUP personnel are in a very big hurry to get rid of these facilities, and by extension divest themselves of any responsibility for the persons who had up until then been detained in those facilities, and that a means that they, in a very accelerated and - certainly from the VRS's perspective - rushed manner, transferred hundreds of individuals, probably thousands, to the VRS's jurisdiction. In my report on page 83, I refer to some communication starting in paragraph 292 in which officials of the Manjaca detention camp, which was clearly a VRS detention facility, expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which they are now being asked to take over full responsibility for detainees being transferred from RS MUP detention facilities, chief of which was here Omarska. They are unhappy on a number of points. One is the physical state of the prisoners when they arrive at Manjaca, and I refer to that in paragraph 292. And they are also unhappy with the fact that the vast majority of these prisoners, as I state in subsequent paragraphs, arrive without any accompanying documentation that would indicate to the VRS why these persons were still being detained. And there's a number of documents from the VRS to the RS MUP, and indeed to the RS government, complaining about the lack of accompanying documentation regarding these prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. I want to go now to 65 ter number 307. This should be tab 38 in your binder. That may be binder 2. We'll start with the first page of this document which is dated 27 July 1992. The signature and stamp appear to be from the minister of Internal Affairs; it's signed but I can't read whose signature it is. Looking at the first page in both English and B/C/S, you see the introductory paragraph says: "Pursuant to the order by the president of the Presidency ..." I take it Radovan Karadzic at the time.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "... as well as the request by the Assembly of the Serbian people in a session held on the 25th and 26th, I issue the following orders:" Now, you've seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what order of the president of the Presidency it refers to and what that was about?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, I've certainly seen the order to which it refers at an earlier point. However, and I have to ask for the Court's understanding on this point, it's a number of years since I prepared this report and, given my other responsibilities, I haven't been able to review every single document that I reviewed originally in preparing this report, so I would want to before making any observations about that order, want to look at the actual order, which, as I said, looked at a number of years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Let me ask the question this way: One of the items -- one of the orders is number 4, which says: "All special units formed during the war period on the territories of the Security Services Centres are to be immediately disassembled and put at disposal of the army." Was that an issue that was either discussed at the Assembly or subject of the order of the president?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I'm aware of the fact that in the Assembly sessions which I was able to review again a number of years ago, there were a frequent number of discussions in the summer of 1992 concerning Special Police units at which concern was expressed about first the proliferation of Special Police units in the RS. At some point it seemed certainly also to members of the Assembly that anyone could form a unit and call it a Special Police unit, and this was a point of concern. And secondly, there was a particular concern with respect to the area of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, ARK, about the activities of the CSB Banja Luka Special Police unit. What one sees in the period pursuant -- or after 27 July 1992, the date this document, is indeed that most of these special units, certainly the ones at the municipality level are shut down. The CSB special units are to a large extent disbanded, at least temporarily, and they are in the course of the second half of 1992, and in accordance with instructions issued by the leading officials of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the RS, reconstituted as a centralised Special Police unit of the RS MUP that is controlled by the commander of that unit and the minister, and which is broken up geographically into several regional units under central control.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Based on your review of the documents, was one of the complaints in particular about the special unit from Banja Luka related to allegations that they committed murders in Kotor Varos at the hospital, murders of non-Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: There were a number of allegations -- sorry, I just started to get the B/C/S in my headphones here. There were a number of allegations made against that unit including alleged killings of civilians as well as the more common allegation which was the plundering or theft of civilians in the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you about item number 2 in this document: "In accordance with my order strictly," number such and such, "dated 23 July, I order that all individuals who were held responsible for crimes and are being officially prosecuted (except for political and verbal offences) are to be immediately removed from the Ministry of Internal Affairs, as well as those persons who had, during the war on the territory of former Bosnia and Herzegovina, committed crimes and for familiar reasons criminal proceedings were not instigated against them." My first question, can you look at the B/C/S and tell me if this translation I have comports with your reading of it, "committed crimes and for familiar reasons criminal proceedings were not instigated against them"?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it could be translated as for familiar reasons or for known reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you, based on your review of the documents, have an idea of what that's of reference to, what might be those known or familiar reasons that certain individuals who had committed crimes during the war and criminal proceedings had not been instigated against them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Based on my review of this and other documents, I can only tentatively conclude that this is a reference to the lack of a fully functioning state, and that, therefore, for known reasons, whatever that in the minister's mind subsumes or includes, has not been possible to conduct criminal proceedings against them, these individuals. I would note, however, that the draft 1992 annual RS MUP report gives very precise figures on, number one, how many employees of RS MUP were removed from the ranks of RS MUP and put at the disposal of the VRS because of conduct perceived to be incompatible with their employment in RS MUP. And that is a figure that is in the thousands, I believe it's above 6.000. The second category are the -- those employees who, in the course of 1992, are removed from RS MUP and are not put at the disposal of the Ministry of Internal Affairs; that is to say, they are removed but they don't go to the VRS -- excuse me, I said Ministry of Internal Affairs, I meant the Ministry of Defence, that is the VRS. That is a quite small number of people by comparison. And the draft 1992 annual RS MUP report also gives figures on the number of police officers who became the subject of criminal proceedings. Likewise, that number which is the exact number is found in the RS MUP draft annual report is much smaller than the number of people who are simply removed and transferred to duty in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise to my learned friend and to the Dr. Nielsen, it is page -- while we are still on the same document, it's page 72, line 20, my learned friend, Mr. Hannis, ask Dr. Nielsen about the item 2 in this document, and it seems to us that there are slight error in translation of the document, so I kindly ask -- we are very lucky to have Dr. Nielsen who is familiar with the B/C/S language, I think it's a proper time to clarify this particular sentence which is actually, Dr. Nielsen, item 2 and then after word "Bosnia and Herzegovina" until the end. And you can compare or my learned friend can clarify that with you, you can compare translation which is on the left side of the screen and this particular sentence, because it's quite important and it changes the substance of this item. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you able to help us with that, Dr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, I've looked at the translation and I've looked at the B/C/S and focusing, I believe, counsel referred to the words after Bosnia and Herzegovina in that last sentence of paragraph 2, and I must say that I do not necessarily have a problem with the official translation we have here. So I would certainly appreciate any clarification. I would note that in -- when there was an issue about the translation of documents in my previous testimony at this Tribunal, I was sometimes asked just to read the passage in B/C/S aloud and then the courtroom interpreters could offer their interpretation of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't have any particular. But thank you, Dr. Nielsen, we shall clarify that in our cross-examination. It was a small test of your knowledge of B/C/S. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, then I'm through with that document. I want to go to the next -- to the last one I have for you, which is 65 ter number 1888. It's tab 45 in your binder. While it's coming up, I'll indicate this is a document dated 20 August 1992. It's a summary of a MUP management Working Group meeting held in Trebinje. Do you have it, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to ask you about an entry on page 6 of the English, and I'm trying to find the reference in B/C/S. It's near the bottom of page 6 in the English concerning the situation in Bijeljina, and I think that's found at page 7 of the B/C/S, near the bottom. No, page 8 of the B/C/S. I didn't allow for the cover page. Do you see that reference, it talks about: "The problem with the Muslim section of the population is compounded by the arrival of Mujezinovic refugees and the return of those who had left Bijeljina before, influenced by Mr. Karadzic's and Mr. Panic's recent statements." And then it goes on, the last sentence in the paragraph: "The misunderstandings between the MUP and the representatives of the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly have partially been resolved following a meeting attended by the minister of the interior." Based on your review of the documents, do you know what that is referring to? Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Panic's statements, the misunderstanding between the MUP and the Bijeljina Municipal Assembly, noting that this is a meeting on 20 August 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Not specifically, no. I know from general knowledge that during this particular time was some notion that at a locality, I believe called Janja, close to Bijeljina there was a remaining enclave of Bosnian Muslims. I can only speculate that it may refer to that, but I'm not able to offer any further comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me take you then to page 10 of the B/C/S, and it's page 8 of the English. Actually on the preceding page in the English it starts out with the minister summarising the discussion and then we can go to page 8 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 10, or the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Item number 4, it mentions that: "The MUP is still receiving requests for active participation on the frontlines." And it says: "That's why in this phase of the creation of our state, our function should also be to protect borders but in accordance with appropriate orders," and then in parentheses we see "co-operation with military commands, activation of a certain number of police employees, own command staff to command at front lines." How do you read the last phrase: "... own command staff to command at front lines" in connection with that earlier 15 May 1992 document we saw creating war units?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: The way I read the portion in parentheses in point 4 is as being compatible with the 15 May 1992 order, which, as I said earlier, reads that the RS MUP units when subordinated to the VRS for the purpose of combat activities are being commanded directly by the designated employees of the ministry for the purpose of that operation, so this would seem to be an illustration of that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next paragraph, the last phrase, it says: "In future a written report must be sent to the minister of the interior on each and every days of police engagement in combat activities." You find that consistent with what you described before about sort of the bureaucratically speaking desire to maintain control over your employees?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I do find that is consistent with my earlier point. I would also point out that the draft 1992 RS MUP annual report as well as the documents sent to the ministry from the regional CSBs at the end of 1992 illustrate that RS MUP officials at municipal, regional, and ministerial level were in the habit of painstakingly collecting information on the number of military operations in which police officials have been involved, the amount of man-hours or man days that had been spent on such combat operations, and that they were in the habit of then collating that information so that the minister and other leading officials could understand the extent to which their employees were involved in one activity or the other. That is to say, whether they were involved in, for example, traffic policing, combatting property crime, or for that matter fighting on the front. Therefore, again, this is consistent in the sense that once a particular combat activity would be concluded, then the minister is reminding everyone here that he wants a written report about every case of further engagement of employees in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Nielsen. Going to the next page in the B/C/S, staying on the same English page, item number 5, starts out: "When conducting their duties, police officers cannot take any sides, despite the demands and attempts at this stage of establishing municipal and republican authorities. Their work must only be based in law." That last sentence reads: "We must fully support each and every one of our members, even when they overstep the bounds of lawful authority to a limited degree." Do you have any idea what that is a reference to concerning members of the MUP overstepping bounds of lawful authority?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I think like everyone, I can only read what it says on the page in the case of the statement. Any further observations I could make would be conjecture. I would just say that there is certainly a later statement from Tomislav Kovac, assistant minister for police, that people, the public in the RS should not jump to conclusions when they, for example, see employees of the ministry removing household goods from houses or taking cars and using it because what that activity which may prima facie appear to be illegal to average citizen, he says, may just simply be RS MUP requisitioning equipment for operational purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Staying on this page in B/C/S and going to the next page in the English, I want to ask but item number 7. And it begins stating: "The order to disband the so-called special units established by CSBs and SJBs, has been issued due to certain abuses." And I think you commented about this earlier, some of the kinds of complaints about special units. Goes on to say: "Criteria for detachment membership must be made stricter." And the last sentence under number 7, says: "Individuals and groups within our ranks," it says "out ranks," but "our ranks shall bear full responsibility under the law for any behaviour to the contrary (genocide, creation of camps, et cetera)." Are you aware from the documentation was there anything indicating that MUP members had been involved in genocide or creation of camps that would cause this to be inserted in this summary of the discussions at the 20 August meeting?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, I am aware of the fact that particularly around the 20 August meeting there were a number of complaints being filed by the VRS regarding the inappropriate treatment in the view of the VRS of the detainees that were being delivered from RS MUP controlled facilities to VRS facilities. I referred to that a bit earlier in the case of the VRS Captain Dana Lukajic [phoen] who is cited in my report and who complains about this -- the treatment of prisoners who are now being transferred from Omarska to Manjaca. I'm also aware of the fact that the VRS in this -- at this particular point in time, and I'd like to just quickly check the date on this. That at this particular point in time there were also allegations that dated from June to August of improper conduct by police officers in the CSB Banja Luka Special Police unit. I think this would be an appropriate moment to note that since the very same point of this document, point 7, states that there were problems with the special units formed at the CSB and SJB levels earlier, and that they are being replaced, as I said earlier, by the centralised detachment of the police of MUP which would be located at various CSBs but would be under a unified command, it's significant to note - as I do in my report - that the CSB Banja Luka police unit, Special Police unit was to a very considerable extent formed out of a previously existing paramilitary organisation; namely, the Serb Defence forces or SOS, and that as such the RS MUP appeared to have had a negative experience with the conduct of paramilitary units -- of paramilitary unit members who had been given permission to act as members of a Special Police unit in the ARK area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, I only have two more documents to show you. One is 65 ter number 1862. It's tab number 66 in your binder. This is a document that previously had the incorrect ERN, and I requested the Court's permission to substitute the correct one which is now on the screen. And, Dr. Nielsen, you talked about this document in your report in reference to a special unit that existed at the level of the headquarters in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, but there was a unit, there was a special unit that existed at the level of the MUP of the RS since the beginning of the conflict, and that is then reconsolidated in the fall of 1992 in a different composition, and with additional control over these regional Special Police units that are at the CSB level. The one that we have in front of us in tab 66, is a payroll from April 1992 and refers to a special detachment that is located at the Serbian MUP, that is to say, at the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My English translation says special platoon. Can you tell me if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That's what I read the B/C/S as saying as well, special platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we've heard evidence before about the special unit or the Special Brigade, the one that was commanded by Milenko Karisik, is this part of that or is this something different?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Well, in this particular case - and I believe this may be the only such payroll for this unit that I've seen - there's not any indications in the document whether or not it is subordinate to another unit. It does say that it's directly at the level of Serbian MUP which would be their term at that point in time for RS MUP, and it say that Dusko Malovic is the commander. There are no references to the existing Special Police unit of RS MUP, which at that point was simply called the special detachment or detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Based on your review of documents, do you have any knowledge about what duties Dusko Malovic and his special platoon performed for the MUP or in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: I know that I refer at one point but only once in the report to Dusko Malovic, but I wouldn't be able to find that part of my report immediately, but it is also the only time that I refer to it and it's not a unit which left an extensive documentary trace, so I'm not in a position to say anything more than what I've already said in the report about that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And let's move then to the final document I'd like to show you. It's tab 80. Tab 80 in your binder. And the 65 ter number is 279. This is document described as a draft report or the RS MUP annual report for 1992 for work in the period April to December 1992. It's dated January 1993 from Bijeljina. And is this the document you referred to a few times earlier in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about a few -- trying to ask you about a few points in here. The first one is on page 6 of the English, and I believe it's page 9 of the B/C/S. Yes. In the English, I'm looking at the bottom of page 6, and this is talking about Eastern Herzegovina. It says: "In that period the work of the Muslim personal in the SJB was blocked and orders and decisions of the official MUP in Sarajevo were refused, all aimed at preparing for a final separation from the BH MUP. The organisation of a Serbian ministry and setting up a CSB based in Trebinje was rushed forward. In February and March, comprehensive activities were conducted in order to set up the Serbian SJB in Mostar and plans were made to break up the Mostar CSB." Skipping to the next sentence and going on to page 7 in the English: "By March, four police stations were set up within the Serbian SJB in Mostar, the take-over of which was planned after signing the oath in the Trebinje CSB. Furthermore, at the end of March 1992 in all the public security stations in the SAO Herzegovina, reserve and active policemen and management staff of Muslim and Croatian background were disarmed." Is that consistent with one of the examples you gave to indicate why you thought the split and formation of a separate Serbian MUP was not part of any Cutileiro discussion or negotiation or plan?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is one of the points on which I based that conclusion, that is correct. It is important to understand that there's no -- despite the 31 March dispatch of 1992 of Momcilo Mandic announcing the establishment of RS MUP on the 1st of April, there is no one answer to the question when did RS MUP truly begin to function on a de facto basis. What we see, as is the case with military units, as is the case with the Crisis Staffs, is we see a variety of events taking place that the date on which the RS MUP starts to function, the date on -- or the date on which Serbian personnel take de facto control of the police in a municipality, is heavily dependent upon local circumstances. But it is in the case, as we see here in Trebinje, it's the case in certainly other areas of Eastern Herzegovina, hence the reference to SAO Herzegovina here, and it's the case in certain other municipalities that long before the Cutileiro negotiations had reached the point at which we have the principles document of 18 March 1992, facts were being, so to speak, constructed on the ground by -- through arming of the police, and through in some cases an unwillingness to continue to co-operate with police officials of other ethnicities. And in some cases, this is also the case in Pale, SJB Pale, outside of Sarajevo, by the removal, firing of Muslim officials or the removal physically from the police station prior to the inauguration of RS MUP. When we speak about Trebinje and Eastern Herzegovina, it's worth noting that in the draft 1992 annual report, they also emphasise that as early as the fall of 1991, September/October 1991, a number of SJBs in Eastern Herzegovina sent ethnic Serb employees of SR BiH MUP to fight on the front in Dubrovnik in Croatia, and they emphasised that they did this and undertook this action despite the fact that it was, in their own words, illegal and despite the fact that no instructions for such mobilisation or combat deployment of police forces had been issued by Sarajevo and by the ministry in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go to the next page in the B/C/S, and near the bottom of page 7 in the English currently on the screen. Reading from the paragraph that says: "It is not our intention to provide an elaborate description of the activities of Serbian employees in the former MUP in organising and enabling of the MUP in the Serbian areas," and I want to go on to the next paragraph. It says: "This applies first and foremost to issues dealing with activities regarding the division of the MUP, illegal organisation of the Serbian MUP at the place where it was based, illegal arming of reliable active personnel and reserve employees, winning over some employees for work in Serbian MUP, preparation for the final division which, to a certain extent, came to a head with the telegram sent to all personnel for their decision to work for the Serbian MUP (at the end of March), preparation of the Law on Internal Affairs and its adoption at the Assembly, splitting of the special purpose unit, liberation of the school at Vraca..." et cetera. First of all, would you agree with me that all events listed there are key events in the creation of a separate Serbian MUP in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: Yes, they are key events and course the report itself sees fit to highlight them because they are in the perspective of the authors of the report key events.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as you've noted before, it uses the reference "illegal organisation" and "illegal arming" to refer to the activities carried out by Serbian MUP personnel earlier in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. And again without taking any analytical position on whether these activities in fact were illegal or not, I again find it significant to highlight that these are employees of the Ministry of Internal Affairs who certainly know what is legal and what is illegal who are making an observation about the illegality of their activities. Moving aside from the issues at hand and the concrete events being described here, one can say as a simple point of logic, that if there truly had been a negotiated agreement or plan, if you will, to split Bosnian MUP up into three ethnically-based MUPs, then why would anyone be engaged in such pervasive and consistent illegal activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I alert you that we are two minutes away from the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to report I don't think I'm going to be able to finish the document in two minutes, but I will be well under my six hours, I may need 20 minutes in the morning to complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Should we take the break at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This would be a good place to break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, what I am going to say I'm sure you will have heard previously, but I'm obliged to remind you that having been sworn as a witness, you cannot, until you are released, have any communication with the lawyers from either side, nor can you discuss your testimony with anyone outside of the court. Unless there is a change of which I am not aware, we will resume tomorrow morning in Courtroom I. So we take the adjournment now to tomorrow morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of December 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
